key_insight: The first U.S. CADASIL natural history cohort establishes a well-characterized baseline of clinical, cognitive, MRI, and biomarker features in carriers of pathogenic NOTCH3 variants versus family controls.
clinical_relevance: This creates a standardized rare-disease model for understanding vascular cognitive impairment and for preparing future trials in small-vessel disease.
method: Cross-sectional baseline analysis from 12 U.S. sites (Oct 2022–Jan 2025)
Adults from families with documented NOTCH3 variants underwent standardized clinical, cognitive, functional, MRI, and proteomic assessments
Comparisons used Fisher’s exact/Kruskal-Wallis tests with multivariable adjustment for age, sex, race, and education
evidence_signal: Among 560 enrolled participants, the analytic cohort included 343 CADASIL carriers and 116 non-carrier family controls, with carriers stratified into low-, medium-, and high-risk NOTCH3 tiers.
watch_item: Findings are baseline and cross-sectional, so they describe association and phenotype distribution rather than disease progression or treatment effect.
paper_title: The United States CADASIL Consortium: Baseline Findings from a Natural History Study
